title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: HOLLIS GETS UP
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Hollis Pelkey, a heating oil driver in Bangor, Maine.
All winter, he keeps half the town warm.
Then he sinks into his recliner and does not move until spring.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE CHECKUP
segments.quote: Above all, do not lose your desire to walk.
segments.author: Soren Kierkegaard
lines: His doctor frowned at his blood pressure and said, Walk. Every day.
Hollis said, Doc, I walk to the truck.
His wife Donna taped a note to the TV remote, from the Danish thinker Soren Kierkegaard:
Above all, do not lose your desire to walk.
Hollis had lost his around nineteen ninety-eight. He laced up anyway.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FIRST LIGHT
segments.quote: The sun himself is weak when he first rises, and gathers strength and courage as the day gets on.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: Six in the morning, eight degrees. He made it to the mailbox, wheezing like an old accordion.
Donna handed him coffee and read from Charles Dickens:
The sun himself is weak when he first rises, and gathers strength and courage as the day gets on.
Next day, the neighbor's mailbox. Then the corner. Then the church.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: FACE FIRST
segments.quote: Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: By January, Donna had signed him up for the Moonlight Snowshoe Race on Pushaw Lake, for the fire department.
On his first try, he stepped on his own snowshoe and fell face first into a drift.
Arlette, a seventy-four-year-old retired game warden, pulled him out laughing and quoted Oscar Wilde:
Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
Then she showed him how. Wide steps, high knees, walk like a proud duck.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: WHOOPIE PIES
segments.quote: To begin is half the work.
segments.author: Ausonius
lines: In February, the scale didn't budge. Hollis quit, and ate six whoopie pies in one sitting.
Arlette found him on the couch and quoted Ausonius, an old Roman poet:
To begin is half the work.
Hollis said, I already began once. She said, Then begin again.
At dawn, he was back on the lake.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: RACE NIGHT
segments.quote: He who limps is still walking.
segments.author: Stanislaw Jerzy Lec
lines: Race night, the frozen lake glowed with three hundred headlamps.
At mile two, a blister felt like a hot penny. He wanted to quit.
Then he remembered a line from the Polish writer Stanislaw Jerzy Lec:
He who limps is still walking.
So he limped. He finished two hundred and eighty-ninth, and the fire chief hugged him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE WALKING CREW
segments.quote: A friend is one who knows you and loves you just the same.
segments.author: Elbert Hubbard
lines: Now Arlette, Donna and four neighbors knock on his door at six every morning.
On his fridge hangs a card from Arlette, quoting Elbert Hubbard:
A friend is one who knows you and loves you just the same.
His blood pressure is down. His recliner misses him terribly.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Walk. Start small. Learn. Begin again. Keep going. Bring friends.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Want to walk. Start small. Learn from the falls. Begin again. Keep limping. Bring friends.
I tried snowshoes once. The rescue dog was very kind about it.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
